newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH GOVT AGENCY SAYS PLANS TO SELL SKODA STAKE.
newsitem.headline: CZECH GOVT AGENCY SAYS PLANS TO SELL SKODA STAKE.

text.p: The Czech government privatisation agency, the National Property Fund (NPF), said on Wednesday it was planning to sell 8.7 percent stake it holds in engineering concern Skoda a.s. soon.
NPF spokesman told Reuters the stake would probably be sold on the capital market within weeks if no property restitution claims appeared which could block it.
"If we find no reason (to block the sale), we will sell it, probably on the capital market," said spokesman Milos Ruzicka.
He added that the stake was originally witheld from privatisation in case of restitution claims, but was freed up after the cabinet unblocked the shares earlier this year.
Ruzicka said the NPF was not aware of any reasons which could prevent the fund from selling the stake.
Skoda's largest shareholder is NERo s.r.o., owned by Skoda General Director Lubomir Soudek. He has expressed an interest to add the NPF stake to his current 21.5 percent holdings in Skoda.
Komercni Banka a.s. holds 11.7 percent together with one of its investment funds. Bank IPB a.s. holds a 5.9 percent stake.
The company is the coutnry's largest engineering concern, based in the western city of Plzen. It is no longer affiliated with Volkswagen AG's Czech unit, car maker Skoda Automobilova a.s. .
Skoda's production range spreads from beer cans to trucks and nuclear reactors.
Skoda shares rose five crowns in Wednesday's Prague Stock Exchange fixing to 1,070.
